據報，Apple has reportedly ramped up its orders for vapor chambers, suggesting the cooling technology could play a bigger role in its future hardware lineup. Here are the details.

Apple bets bigger on vapor chamber cooling

Leaker Fixed Focus Digital on Weibo claimed that Apple "significantly increased its total orders for vapor chambers," and said this "could be preparing for enhanced cooling in its first foldable iPhone and next-generation 20th anniversary model."

Apple first introduced vapor chamber cooling with the iPhone 17 Pro, a change that helped address thermal issues from previous generations.

Vapor chambers work by evaporating a small amount of liquid near the heat source, condensing it in cooler areas to spread the heat over a larger surface, and then letting the liquid flow back to repeat the cycle.

You can see how this works in action in this excellent video from Know Art:

While the Weibo post speculated that Apple's increased orders were for the rumored iPhone Ultra and a 20th anniversary iPhone expected in 2027, the timing makes more sense for this year's lineup.

Apple has reportedly asked suppliers to prepare around 10 million foldable iPhones, up from a previous target of 7 to 8 million, as well as about 70 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units. All three models are expected to use vapor chamber cooling.

The increase comes amid reports that Apple has resolved earlier hinge and yield issues, paving the way for higher production ahead of a September launch.
